change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: website_name leaks TL0 users' website to anonymous visitors, bypassing untrusted_attributes
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous visitor `include_website?` returns false (lines 28-31, `restrict_user_fields?` in lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60). `website_name` gets no such filter. It is not in `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializers never calls it as an include filter; it's dead code. The result: an anonymous visitor (or a crawler) looking at a TL0 spam account gets `website_name: "spam-site.com"`, and user.hbs:66-71 renders it in the profile header. That's the exact thing the TL0 restriction exists to stop. Fix: delete `include_website_name` and add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`. Its generated `include_website_name?` already checks `present?`. Also add `website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 so a test covers this.

findings.title: Website name goes stale after the user edits their website in preferences
findings.body: Before this change, `websiteName` was computed from `model.website`, so it updated as soon as the user saved preferences. Now the template reads `model.website_name`, a value the server sends only through `findDetails()` in the `user` route's `afterModel` (routes/user.js.es6:50-58). `preferences` is a child route of `user` (app-route-map.js.es6:56,74), and `User#save` (models/user.js.es6:206-213) copies only `bio_excerpt` back from the response. So when a user changes their website and goes back to their profile, the header still shows the old name, or nothing if they just added a website, next to an `href` that points to the new URL. A full reload is the only fix. Set `website_name` from the PUT response the way `bio_excerpt` is set, if the update endpoint returns a serialized user. Otherwise keep a client-side fallback.

findings.title: Port is dropped from the displayed website name
findings.body: The old client code (`website.split("/")[2]`) showed `example.com:8080` for `http://example.com:8080/`. `URI#host` drops the port, so the name now shows `example.com` while the link goes to port 8080. If the change is meant to keep the old display for foreign domains, consider using `URI#host` plus the port when it isn't the default.

findings.title: Sibling-domain heuristic treats unrelated domains under a public suffix as the same site
findings.body: This branch removes the first label and compares what's left. With three-label hosts under a multi-part public suffix, unrelated sites match: a website on `foo.co.uk` and a forum on `bar.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`, so the full path is shown as if the website belonged to the forum's domain. The effect is only cosmetic, but the heuristic doesn't do what the comment `www.example.com == forum.example.com` says. A stricter rule would be a public-suffix check, or requiring the remainder to have at least 2 labels plus a non-ccTLD second-level label.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain branch and the TL0 case are untested
findings.body: The three new examples cover the equal-host branch (line 141) and the `ends_with?` branch (line 149). None of them covers the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch at user_serializer.rb:144-146. The TL0/anonymous example at lines 6-15 doesn't check `website_name` either, which is why the leak reported on user_serializer.rb:153 went unnoticed.

contracts.action: New serialized attribute website_name rendered in the profile header instead of the client-computed websiteName
contracts.equivalent_path: website attribute, filtered by untrusted_attributes for TL0 users seen anonymously
contracts.before_after: Before: the client derived websiteName from model.website, which was already hidden for restricted users, so nothing showed. After: website_name is always serialized because include_website_name lacks `?` and the attribute is not in untrusted_attributes, so restricted users' website hosts reach anonymous viewers.
contracts.visible_effect: user.hbs shows model.website_name text, linked to model.website
contracts.failure_mode: URI parse errors are rescued and return nil, so nothing is shown

contracts.action: Profile header after the user saves a changed website in preferences
contracts.equivalent_path: User#save then navigating back to the user's profile
contracts.before_after: Before: websiteName was a computed property of model.website and updated right away. After: website_name loads once in the user route's afterModel and isn't refreshed by save or by moving between child routes.
contracts.visible_effect: The name stays stale (or missing) until a full reload, while href points at the new website

summary: This change moves the website display name from the client to the server, and the new attribute skips the protection on `website`. Anonymous visitors (and crawlers) can now see the website of a TL0 (trust level 0) user, because `website_name` isn't in `untrusted_attributes` and `include_website_name` has no `?`, so it never runs as a filter. That's a blocker. The name also goes stale after a user edits their website in preferences, because it is loaded once per user route and isn't refreshed. Smaller points: the port is now dropped from the name, the sibling-domain heuristic can match unrelated domains, and two branches lack tests.
